details.summary: This is an outstanding recipe that hits every requirement. It uses smart, accessible shortcuts like microwave brown rice and frozen edamame to deliver a fast, satisfying, plant-protein-forward meal completely aligned with the dietary guidelines.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is classic and balanced. Soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil create a coherent, umami-rich sauce that perfectly complements tofu and broccoli.
Every listed ingredient is accounted for in the steps, and no unlisted ingredients appear.
Instructions are excellent. Cook times are provided as ranges, every step has a minimum-time check instruction, and there are clear visual cues ('golden brown', 'bright green', 'liquid reduces').
The ingredients and techniques flawlessly align with an easy Asian-American stir-fry.
Skillet stir-frying is the ideal method for cooking extra-firm tofu and quick-cooking vegetables like broccoli.
The computed macros perfectly match the ingredients. The 32.1g of protein makes sense given the large portions of tofu and edamame.
The title is accurate, and the intro provides excellent, practical context on 'stacking plant proteins' without resorting to medicalized jargon or banned claims.
Highly appealing. It's a colorful, fast, and familiar weeknight staple that readers will actively want to cook.
Nails the brief for both conditions: uses extra-virgin olive oil as the primary cooking fat, provides a high-quality whole grain, and features substantial plant protein and fiber.
Zero added sugar, and the dish successfully provides a real, high-quality carbohydrate base (brown rice) that lands perfectly inside the 32-55g target window for a healthy blood-sugar response.
Flawlessly hits the 'Vegetable & Meatless Dinners' brief. It achieves the challenging target of >=26g protein in a vegan meal by smartly combining tofu and edamame.
Easily achievable in under 30 minutes from a cold start. Using a microwave brown rice pouch and frozen shelled edamame are perfect, book-approved shortcuts.
